title: Integrability of a centered coordinate square
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, let $c=(c_j)_{j\in I}\in\mathbb R^I$, let $v\ge0$, and choose $i\in I$. Under the product measure whose $j$th coordinate has Gaussian distribution with mean $c_j$ and variance parameter $v$, the function $z\mapsto(z_i-c_i)^2$ is integrable.
replaced: For a finite set $I$, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v\ge0$, and $i\in I$, the function $z\mapsto(z_i-c_i)^2$ is integrable under $\bigotimes_jN(c_j,v)$.
